text:
The summary gets most facts right: 347 statements, the exposed data types, no external access, the regulator notification on 3 October, member contact by 6 October, the fixes and their dates, and the 9 October send date. It stays under 120 words.

However, "stopped after 35 minutes" is not supported by the source. The report gives the stop time (9:35am) but not when the job started, so the duration is an inference presented as fact. The summary also omits the all-staff "we've been hacked" message, which was forwarded externally and quoted in the news, and the planned fix to incident communications. A manager would likely want both, since they bear on reputational risk and on what staff were told. The summary does correctly flag "not a hack" in its title and lists the deletion request nowhere, which is a minor gap.

Overall, the accuracy is good apart from one unsupported figure, and the concision is good, but it drops a meaningful governance point.

Score: 6
